focus: Mark treatment for lines, areas, bars and fills
noveltyJustification: This iteration isolates signed polarity and density-aware point disclosure as the two mark-level gaps while confirming that the shipped line, stack and baseline geometry should remain the default.
keyQuestions: Which mark treatments are genuinely missing or weak after the shipped phases 15 to 19?
answeredQuestions: The shipped register is coherent. Add per-form sparse-dot and meaningful-zero signed-area policies, while retaining current line weight, flat stack separators, gap handling and baseline-anchored columns.
ruledOut: Global visible points on every line and area.
Universal smooth interpolation or gradient fills for stacked composition.
Rounding the baseline end of quantitative columns.
Adding a new external mark family to the catalog solely because it appears in the reference library.

title: Shipped line, area and bar register is coherent
summary: The current 2px line, restrained single-area fade, flat separated stack and baseline-anchored columns cover common questions without a global mark reset.

title: Sparse series need an explicit point policy
summary: Transparent hit circles preserve interaction but hide point density. A per-form sparse-dot policy is useful, while dense daily lines should remain dotless by default.

title: Signed area around a meaningful zero is missing
summary: The current area closes every run to one baseline treatment. A signed form should split positive and negative fills only when zero is semantically meaningful.

title: Flat separated stack fills should remain
summary: The existing 0.4 fills, 2px surface separators and four-series capacity guard keep composition and identity distinct. A universal gradient would add ambiguity.

title: Baseline-anchored column geometry is correct
summary: Rounding only the free end preserves quantitative contact with the baseline. Fully rounded reference bars do not justify changing this default.

title: Curve, label and density choices belong to individual forms
summary: Smooth curves, in-band labels, grouped bars and dense monochrome areas are valid specialized variants but should not become global defaults or new catalog families without a question.

direction: Global visible points on every line and area.
reason: The current daily line intentionally uses transparent circles as hit regions and reserves the visible point for the emphasized datum; references present dots as a variant for sparse or point-oriented data.

direction: Universal smooth interpolation or gradient fills for stacked composition.
reason: Curve and fill choices carry data meaning. A smooth or gradient stack could imply values between observations and compete with series identity.

direction: Rounding the baseline end of quantitative columns.
reason: The baseline is the measurement anchor, so the free-end-only path keeps the column in contact with its scale.

direction: Adding LayerChart, Unovis or another external mark family to the catalog solely because the library contains it.
reason: The question-first catalog already maps the shipped forms and reserves specialized missing-form decisions for the final angle.
